units.source_text: 此时明石道人弹起那音色特别美好的筝来，技法非常高明，源氏公子深为感动。

en.t: At that moment, the Akashi monk began to play a koto of especially beautiful tone, and his skill was so superb that Prince Genji was deeply moved.

units.source_text: 筝这乐器，若教女子从容不迫、自由自在地弹奏，真好听呢。”

en.t: The koto is truly lovely when a woman plays it calmly and freely."

units.source_text: 明石道人不觉莞尔而笑，答道：“

en.t: The Akashi monk could not help smiling, and replied, "

units.source_text: 听了公子的演奏之后，哪里还有女子弹得更好听呢？

en.t: After hearing Your Highness play, how could any woman play it more beautifully?

units.source_text: 实不相瞒：弹筝之道，我家受延喜帝嫡传，至今已历三代了。

en.t: To tell the truth, the art of playing the koto was passed directly to my family from Emperor Engi, and it has now continued for three generations.

units.source_text: 我身命运不济，早已摒除世俗之事。

en.t: My own fortunes have been poor, and I long ago set aside worldly affairs.

units.source_text: 但偶逢心情不快之时，也常弹筝遣怀。

en.t: Yet when my heart is troubled, I often play the koto to console myself.

units.source_text: 不料小女也来模仿，听其自习，弹得竟与已故亲王殿下手法相似呢。

en.t: Unexpectedly, my daughter began to imitate me as well, and when I hear her practicing on her own, her playing is surprisingly like that of the late prince.

units.source_text: ——呀，失言了，想是我这‘山僧’耳钝，把琴声当作‘松风音’，故而胡言乱道罢了。

en.t: Ah, I have spoken out of turn. Perhaps this dull-eared mountain monk mistook the sound of the koto for the sound of the wind in the pines, and so babbled nonsense.

units.source_text: 不过我总想找个机会，教公子悄悄地听一听小女弹筝呢。”

en.t: Still, I have always wished to find an opportunity for Your Highness to hear my daughter play the koto in secret."

units.source_text: 他说到这里，全身发抖，几乎流出眼泪来。

en.t: When he had said this much, his whole body trembled, and he was almost moved to tears.
